quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Perioperative Imfinzi plus neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin (09-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AstraZeneca's supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) for Imfinzi (durvalumab) in combination with enfortumab vedotin (EV) was accepted and granted Priority Review by the US FDA for patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) who are ineligible for or have declined cisplatin-based chemotherapy. The PDUFA date is anticipated during the fourth quarter of 2026. The sBLA rests on the VOLGA Phase III trial (695 patients randomised 1:1:1, conducted in 182 centres across 25 countries), whose planned interim analysis showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in event-free survival and overall survival versus radical cystectomy with or without approved adjuvant treatment; the results will be presented at a forthcoming medical meeting. Regulatory applications based on VOLGA are under review in the EU, Japan and several other countries. Imfinzi is already approved in over 50 countries for cisplatin-eligible MIBC (NIAGARA), and more than 470,000 patients have been treated with Imfinzi since its first approval in May 2017. Susan Galbraith (EVP, Oncology Haematology R&D) said that, if approved, this would be the first perioperative regimen with enfortumab vedotin given only before surgery (company claim).
